report.summary: The only failure is tests.api.test_books_api::test_book_can_be_updated, and it is a test bug: the test sends year=2001 but asserts year=2002. The app stores and returns the value it was given, so the fix is to correct the test's expected year (or the request value) and rerun. No product or infrastructure fault is involved.

causes.title: Update test expects a year it never sent
causes.explanation: The test PUTs year=2001 (line 23) and then asserts the fetched book has year=2002 (line 27). The API's PUT handler writes book.year unchanged into the database (app/main.py:232-233) and GET returns row["year"] unchanged (app/main.py:156), so the correct stored value is 2001. The failing assertion is therefore the test's own typo, not an application defect. Nothing in the update path shifts the year. The seeded year_off_by_one bug only relaxes the upper bound in validate_book (app/main.py:94) and does not alter stored values, so it does not explain this failure.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:232-233: "UPDATE books SET title = ?, author = ?, year = ? WHERE id = ?", (book.title, book.author, book.year, book_id)
app/main.py:156: return {"id": row["id"], "title": row["title"], "author": row["author"], "year": row["year"]}
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 27, change "year": 2002 to "year": 2001 so the expected value matches the request. Alternatively, change the request on line 23 to year=2002 if that was the intent. Either way, keep the sent and asserted values identical.
